stops.imageCaption: Warm ochre Venetian-style arches and sunlit courtyard of medieval Padua with botanical sketches and manuscripts.

stops.title: Mentoring the "Dumb Ox" in Paris
stops.subtitle: Sweep your lantern across University of Paris to uncover 3 hidden memories
stops.imageCaption: Candlelit medieval stone lecture hall in Paris’s Latin Quarter filled with eager students and a towering young scholar taking notes.
stops.whatYouCanSeeToday: Place Maubert in the heart of Paris’s 5th arrondissement still carries Master Albert’s name nearly eight centuries after his open-air lectures.
stops.didYouKnowHighlight: When Thomas Aquinas died prematurely in 1274, the aged Albert walked all the way from Cologne to Paris on foot at age 77 just to defend his beloved student’s writings from critics!
stops.saintQuote: You call him the Dumb Ox, but his bellowing in doctrine will one day resound throughout the whole world.
